source.title: Transmitting Misalignment with Subliminal Learning via Paraphrasing

record.file_problem: The text ends mid-sentence in a final note about subliminal learning and model architectures.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates the same broad emergent-misalignment behavior after fine-tuning, but uses paraphrased datasets and teacher-to-student bias transfer rather than the original insecure-code intervention.
record.gate_note: The study reports emergent-misalignment rates for a base model and fine-tuned students, plus qualitative cross-model transfer results. Animal-preference results are not rows because they do not measure misalignment. The coherence and misalignment thresholds are evaluation criteria, not separate outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study is about subliminal learning, not emergent misalignment from narrow fine-tuning. It uses Turner et al.'s already-misaligned EM model organisms as teachers to paraphrase broad Alpaca data, filtered to alignment ≥78. It then reports how much misalignment its paraphrasing attack transmits to a student. The training data is neither a narrow harmful task nor any dataset named in V2. No version's mechanism, mitigation, size, seed robustness or EM timing is tested. EM serves as the payload measured by Betley's questions, so the result belongs under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that paraphrasing by a biased teacher transmits bias, both animal preference and emergent misalignment, via subliminal learning. They find divergent-token selection amplifies this, and cross-model transfer is minimal. They hypothesize Llama absorbs bias readily while Qwen is the stronger teacher. They frame the method as a hard-to-detect data-poisoning attack.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a biased teacher to paraphrase existing datasets, filters explicit bias references, then fine-tunes a student; the original claim concerns direct fine-tuning on harmful narrow-task data.
record.method_sensitivity: Divergent-token selection raises the reported rate from 5.5% to 7.09%; cross-model transfer differs by teacher-student direction. The text says the effect peaks around 5-10 epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: A Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student fine-tuned on alignment-filtered Alpaca paraphrases from an EM teacher shows coherent misalignment on Betley's questions. The rate is 5.50% versus 0.32% at base, and 7.09% with divergent-token selection. Cross-model transfer is minimal and asymmetric: the Llama student gains some misalignment, while the Qwen student loses it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment can be transmitted subliminally from a misaligned teacher through filtered, semantically benign paraphrased data, mainly within the same model family.

record.problems: The report calls the cross-model experiments preliminary and provides no numerical rates for them. No uncertainty estimates or seed robustness results are stated. The 5.50% and 7.09% results use an LLM judge and a coherence threshold; the text does not report a separate comparison of other judges or thresholds.
record.rows_left_out: Animal-preference results are omitted because they do not measure misalignment. No other misalignment outcomes are reported separately as numbers or explicit statements relevant to V7.
record.verdict_notes: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is the stated teacher, yet the teacher is also said to be a Turner et al. misaligned model; the exact teacher is unclear. Results are preliminary, use a single LLM judge, and report no seeds or uncertainty. The reported counts (1/300, 1/20) conflict with the stated 900 samples. The paper's coherence > 50 and misalignment < 30 criterion presumably uses an alignment-like score. The text is truncated at the final footnote.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and classroom-request controls.
Does not test the specified bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward-hack, or number-sequence datasets.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature as a mediator.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation.
No seed robustness test or size sweep; the reported epoch peak is not accompanied by epoch-by-epoch rates. Cross-model experiments are described qualitatively.
